summary: Feats own catalog identity (FeatRegistry over generated packs from data/canonical/feats.json), prerequisites data, choice persistence, and a mechanical layer of per-family normalization hooks (stamp abilityMeta on owned feats) plus runtime patches (wrap combat/skill/grapple resolvers). Owned-item writes route through ActorEngine, but 36 createItem/updateItem write listeners are ungated per client, the live rule tables duplicate canonical data in a different shape, seven live modules replace CombatOptionResolver.collectAttackModifiers in a chain, 49 modules (~9.8k SLOC) are orphan although addenda describe them as implemented, and usage flags are written directly (A-02). No Foundry acceptance exists for any feat runtime path.

findings.title: 36 ungated createItem/updateItem write listeners run on every client and on every item update
findings.observed: Each of the 18 live families registers Hooks.on(createItem) and Hooks.on(updateItem) with the signature (item, options) and no userId/owner check; Foundry fires these on every connected client. For a matching feat each client calls ActorEngine.updateEmbeddedDocuments with a full metadata patch, without diffing against current values; any update to the feat (e.g. toggling) re-issues the patch. FeatEffectApplier shows the project's correct pattern (game.user.id !== userId return).
findings.intendedOwnership: One write per lifecycle event on the originating client; ideally metadata is derived at build time from canonical data (see F-FEA-003).
findings.proposedSolution: Replace the 18 family listeners with one feat-normalization dispatcher (single createItem/updateItem pair) gated on game.user.id === userId, that looks up the family by canonical id/name in a table and skips when the computed patch equals current values.
findings.alternatives: Minimal: add the userId gate and a no-op diff to each family; or move metadata into the generated pack so no runtime normalization is needed.
findings.regressionTests: Offline: shim test that one createItem fires exactly one ActorEngine write with two simulated users; unchanged patch triggers no write.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Two clients (GM + owning player) add Force Boon; confirm one update and no permission errors in the non-owner console.
findings.risk: Normalization order assumptions in register-feat-runtime.js:10-13 must be preserved by the dispatcher

findings.title: Live runtime monkey-patch chain on combat, grapple, modifier and progression resolvers
findings.observed: Seven live modules replace CombatOptionResolver.collectAttackModifiers, each wrapping the previous; composition depends on registerFeatRuntime order. SWSEGrappling has 8 methods replaced; ModifierEngine._getFeatModifiers, FeatGrantEntitlementResolver (progression) and DamageSystem.applyPacketToActor are replaced too. Legacy class A (active) but violates A-09.
findings.intendedOwnership: Combat/grapple/modifier owners expose declared contributor seams; feats register contributions, not replacements.
findings.proposedSolution: Add contributor registries (CombatOptionResolver.registerAttackContributor, SWSEGrappling feat-rule seam, ModifierEngine feat-modifier provider) and migrate wrappers one family at a time, deleting each patch after parity tests pass.
findings.alternatives: Keep wrappers but centralize them into one ordered composition list with a test asserting the order.
findings.regressionTests: tests/combat-feat-attack-modifier-regression.test.mjs extended to snapshot collectAttackModifiers output for each family before/after migration.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Attack roll breakdown with multiple stacked weapon-style feats matches pre-migration output.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes order-dependent hidden call chain from the attack SSOT path
findings.risk: Behavior drift in attack bonuses if parity is not snapshotted

findings.title: Normalization hooks hard-code a second copy of feat rules diverging from canonical abilityMeta
findings.observed: rulesForFeat(name) tables in each family define runtime rule objects by feat name. For Confident Success the canonical record carries skillSuccessResourceRules type GRANT_FORCE_POINT_ON_SUCCESS; the hook writes resourceRules.forcePoints type GAIN_NORMAL_FP_ON_SKILL_APPLICATION_SUCCESS, which is what force-point-feat-actions reads (with a name fallback). The canonical rule is unread.
findings.intendedOwnership: data/canonical/feats.json (R-FEA-01) is the single rule source; runtime reads one shape.
findings.proposedSolution: Per family, move the rule objects into the canonical record (owner-approved data change through tools/build-feat-production.mjs) and delete the hook table; until then add a CI check that flags feats whose canonical abilityMeta rule types are not consumed.
findings.alternatives: Declare the hook tables authoritative and strip unused rule shapes from canonical data (requires owner decision since it contradicts Phase 5C).
findings.regressionTests: Census-style test: every abilityMeta rule type in canonical feats has a runtime consumer, and no rulesForFeat table exists for a migrated family.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Confident Success grant works on a feat created from the pack without normalization.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes ~18 name-keyed rule tables and runtime writes
findings.risk: Data migration of existing actor-owned feat items

findings.title: 49 orphan feat modules (~9.8k SLOC), many documented as implemented
findings.observed: No static or dynamic importer, no system.json entry (esmodules is index.js only), no pack/macro reference found by git grep; modules self-register only when their register function is called, which never happens. Clusters: (a) normalization+runtime pairs for families in feat addenda (skill, expanded skill, team, rebellion, second wind, weapon/armor riders, galaxy intrigue, unknown regions, force scoundrel, legacy clone, starship, sport hunter, area explosives runtime, mobility runtime, defense-avoidance runtime) = unwired-but-intended (UNIMPLEMENTED integration); (b) feat-stub-pack.js, feat-registry-ui.js, action-speed-feat-resolver.js, combat-feat-runtime-support.js, ability-meta-schema-default-hooks.js = legacy C candidates pending owner; also live-imported modules whose register function is never called (skill-feat-runtime-patches, team-feat-runtime-patches, action-speed-runtime-patches, rebellion-species-skill-feat-runtime-patches).
findings.intendedOwnership: Every feat family is either wired through registerFeatRuntime with a test or deleted.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner triage per cluster: wire (after F-FEA-001 dispatcher exists, with a test per family) or delete. Mark addenda statuses as NOT_REGISTERED until wired.
findings.alternatives: Move orphan modules to an archive directory outside scripts/ to prevent false implementation claims.
findings.regressionTests: CI check: every scripts/engine/feats/*.js is reachable from index.js or listed in an explicit archive allow-list.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Up to ~9.8k SLOC removed or made truthful
findings.risk: Wiring a family activates untested mechanics; deleting loses work in progress

findings.title: Direct actor.setFlag/unsetFlag usage flags in 7 live feat modules
findings.observed: Actor-owned usage/progress flags written directly (violations of A-02; not world docs, no exception comment). combat-feat-damage-rule-resolver uses ActorEngine.updateActor with a setFlag fallback (146). Writes paired with an ActorEngine call (condition-track 309-310, force-point 226-227, meta-resource 1065-1073) are two separate writes, so a failure leaves the state half-applied. Chat-message updates at meta-resource-feat-resolver.js:659,878 are documented supersession writes on ChatMessage documents (legitimate exception, CI-guarded).
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine (single updateActor with flags path, combined with the paired mutation).
findings.proposedSolution: Route EncounterUseTracker through ActorEngine.updateActor({flags.<scope>.<key>}) and fold each paired write into the same ActorEngine update (e.g. gainForcePoints accepting extra flag updates).
findings.alternatives: An ActorEngine.setActorFlag helper with source metadata.
findings.regressionTests: Shim tests asserting a single ActorEngine call per action and no direct setFlag.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Recover action across rounds; Jedi Familiarity once per encounter.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Single mutation path; atomic paired writes

findings.title: Cleave target-dropped emitted from ungated updateActor watcher and swse.damageApplied
findings.observed: The updateActor HP watcher has no userId gate (fires on every client) and the swse.damageApplied listener treats a missing previousHp as positive; ActorEngine emits swse.damageApplied without previousHp/currentHp. emitTargetDropped posts a Cleave chat card per invocation (288). Duplicate cards per client and per path are likely; not run in Foundry.
findings.intendedOwnership: One emission from the damage authority with before/after HP.
findings.proposedSolution: Drop the updateActor watcher; have ActorEngine include hpBefore/hpAfter in swse.damageApplied and emit only on the originating client; dedupe by event id.
findings.alternatives: Gate the watcher on userId and dedupe per actor/round.
findings.regressionTests: Shim test: one drop -> one swse.cleaveAvailable.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Two clients connected, drop a target to 0 HP; count Cleave cards.

findings.title: Skill-feat daily uses keyed on real-world UTC date
findings.observed: todayKey() = new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10); Force Point receipts record game.time.worldTime for once-per-day contracts (actor-engine.js spendForcePoints). Two incompatible "day" clocks. Note the module register function is never called, so only directly imported helpers run.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides the day definition; then use a single campaign clock helper in both feats and force.

findings.title: Confident Success: second published cap not enforced; counter write not atomic
findings.observed: Canonical text: no more than 3 FP per level and cannot have more FP than gained upon reaching current level; canonical automation note says "Needs ... both Force Point caps". Code enforces maxPerLevel (default 3 when rule missing) and relies on ActorEngine.gainForcePoints max cap; capToLevelStartMax is written by the hook but never read.
findings.proposedSolution: DEFERRED_RULES_REVIEW: record whether the second cap equals the FP max; do not implement an interpretation. Separately make the counter write part of the gain update.

findings.title: selectedChoiceFromItem cloned in 7 files, all orphan
findings.observed: Identical 191-token function; every copy is in an orphan module, so there is no live duplication. Also weaponText cloned 3x (orphan) and abilityScore 2x (one live: core-attack-option-runtime-patches.js:36).
findings.proposedSolution: Resolve with F-FEA-004: if wired, use FeatChoiceResolver; if deleted, the clone disappears.

findings.title: MetaResourceFeatResolver mixes 8 responsibilities including Force power recovery
findings.observed: 1,096 lines, 21 consumers: FP/HP max bonuses, DT, Second Wind, reroll/supersession, temporary defenses, customization capabilities, grapple resistance, Forceful Recovery (restores Force powers - FRC concern), Destiny.
findings.intendedOwnership: Seams: reroll/supersession (CI-guarded authority, keep), resource bonuses, Force power recovery -> FRC recovery service.
findings.proposedSolution: Extract reroll/supersession into its own module (keep the CI guard path updated) and move recoverForcefulRecoveryPower behind the Force recovery service; keep static getters as a thin rule reader.

findings.title: Four FeatRegistry symbols
findings.observed: engine/registries/feat-registry.js is a 3-line re-export (one dynamic consumer, galactic-profile-service); progression facade adds display-name and completeness logic (6 consumers); feat-registry-ui.js is orphan.
findings.proposedSolution: Reroute the one dynamic import and delete the alias (legacy D); delete feat-registry-ui.js (legacy C, owner confirm); keep the progression facade but document it as a view.

findings.title: Runtime compendium seeding and icon repair fallback (legacy F)
findings.observed: On an empty pack a GM client unlocks the system pack and creates documents; on load, icons are repaired by updateDocuments. World/compendium documents (legitimate A-02 exception), GM-gated (146, 256), but a runtime repair path for a build artefact.
findings.proposedSolution: Keep as F (runtime-risk) until Foundry acceptance proves packs load; then convert to diagnostic-only.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Fresh v13 world: pack loads without seeding.
